Fix HTTP 406 on submit: rename the "format" form field to "talk-format"

Field ids become query parameters on github.com/<repo>/issues/new, and Rails

406 Not Acceptable. Add a reserved-id guard to form.json validation so this
cannot come back.

commits.message:
perf(misc#426): persist scores.last_updated_at and index scores by data call (#609)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#426.

The home dashboard calls `/scores/progress` and `/scores/aggregate` once
per active data call. Both read far more than their output needs. This
cuts that without changing either response, and needs no frontend
change.

## Why

**`/scores/progress`** computed `lastupdatedat` with a `LEFT JOIN
LATERAL` onto `events`, run once per score row (~70k per call), then
collapsed by `MAX()` to one timestamp per system. #437 moved the
progress counts onto `scores.status`, which left this timestamp as the
query's last read of the audit log and the bulk of its cost.

**`/scores/aggregate`** filters `scores` by `datacallid`, but the only
composite index (0061) leads with `fismasystemid`. So every call read
every cycle's rows, and got slower with each new data call.

## What

- **0063** adds a nullable `scores.last_updated_at` with no default, so
carried-forward and imported rows stay NULL.
- **0064** backfills it from `events` using 0048's `created`/`updated`
rule, which yields the same value the lateral computed. It is kept out
of 0063 so that 0063's `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock lasts only for the column
add, not the backfill.
- **0065** adds an index on `scores (datacallid, fismasystemid)`.
- Numbered after #598's `0062`, so this merges after #598.
- `Save` (insert and update) and `Confirm` set `last_updated_at = now()`
in the same statement that sets `status = 'done'`. It is not added to
`RETURNING`, so the `Score` response and the event payload are
unchanged.
- Progress reads `MAX(s.last_updated_at)`, and the lateral is gone. The
seed stamps the column the same way. OpenAPI is regenerated (description
change only).

The stamp records when the score was written, a few ms before its
event's `createdat`. So `lastupdatedat` can differ from a score's
`last_edited_at` by a few ms. A save whose fire-and-forget event write
fails now still gets a timestamp.

## Before merge: Snowflake

The data sync copies every `scores` column into Snowflake, and the
Snowflake `SCORES` table is maintained by hand. **Add `LAST_UPDATED_AT
TIMESTAMP_TZ` (nullable) in DEV, IMPL and PROD before merging.** A merge
deploys DEV and then PROD (#604), and the sync fails on a column its
target table lacks. PR environments don't sync, so marking this ready is
safe.

## Not in this PR: capacity

Aurora Serverless v2 is capped at `max_capacity = 1.0` ACU
(`infrastructure/rds.tf`), and the dashboard's concurrent requests share
it. Raising the cap (to 2–4) is a one-line change and close to
cost-neutral: billing is per ACU-second consumed, `max` is a ceiling
rather than a reservation, and `min` (the idle cost) stays at 0.5. But a
higher cap hides the cost rather than removing it, and wouldn't stop the
aggregate growing each cycle. It is left out deliberately, to revisit
once this deploys and the dashboard is re-measured.

## Testing

- Unit, migration and integration suites pass. `staticcheck` is clean,
and `make generate-openapi` regenerates byte-identical output.
- New: a backfill test. The newest `created`/`updated` event wins,
imported-only and event-less rows stay NULL, and down clears the column.
- Extended:
  - Save on create, edit and no-op.
  - Confirm and re-confirm.
- Carried-forward rows. The source row is now stamped, so the carried
copy's NULL check proves something.
- Prod-scale copy (957 systems, 10 calls, 377k scores):
  - Progress output is identical to the old query.
- Page reads per request dropped from 1,405 to 316 MB for progress, and
from 186 to 137 MB for the aggregate, which now uses an index scan
instead of a full scan.
  - The backfill took 1.8 s.

Drafts that write `scores` (#595, #596) will need their Undo and
transactional write paths to set `last_updated_at` as well.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `last_updated_at` is persisted and written by Save and Confirm
alongside `status = 'done'`. Carried-forward and imported rows stay
NULL.
- [x] Existing rows are backfilled with 0048's `created`/`updated` rule.
- [x] `/scores/progress` no longer reads `events`. The response is
unchanged, with no frontend change.
- [x] `scores` has an index leading with `datacallid`, so the aggregate
no longer reads every cycle's rows.
- [ ] Snowflake `SCORES.LAST_UPDATED_AT` is added in DEV, IMPL and PROD
before merge.

Optional follow-up, not required for this PR: after the PROD deploy,
`VACUUM (FULL, ANALYZE) public.scores;` (via `make db-shell-prod`,
off-hours) reclaims the space this backfill and #594's left behind. The
table is small, so skipping it only costs a little disk.

feat(misc#393): serve questionnaire ordering from the database (#598)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#393, the third ticket in Versioned
Questionnaires (CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#307). Frontend half is
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#741, which **must merge and deploy after this
PR**.

## Why

Migration 0056 moved `pillars.ordr` and `questions.ordr` into the
database but stopped at the functions table: `functions.ordr` was never
populated, and `FindQuestionsByFismaSystem` did not select it. The gap
was filled client-side by `PILLAR_FUNCTION_MAP` in ztmf-ui, which sorts
by function **name**. Rename or add a function and it silently drops to
the bottom of its pillar. #307 makes catalog edits routine, so the order
has to come from the API.

## What

**Backfill (migration 0062).** Data-only; the column has existed since
0004.

```sql
UPDATE functions f
SET ordr = q.ordr
FROM questions q
WHERE q.questionid = f.questionid
  AND coalesce(q.ordr, 0) <> 0
  AND coalesce(f.ordr, 0) = 0;
```

Ranks are copied from the owning question, so every edition of a
function gets the same rank without a second hand-maintained list.
`ordr` is nullable, so the `coalesce` guards are required: a bare
`f.ordr = 0` skips NULL rows. The migration never overwrites a rank
someone set, and its down reverts only the ranks it wrote.

`functions.ordr` ranks the functions within one question. Today each
(question, environment) pair has one function, so they tie and the
`questionid` tiebreaker decides; the column exists so a versioned
catalog can rank a fork without another migration.

**`Function.Ordr` becomes `*int`.** `PUT /functions/{id}` without
`"order"` decoded as 0 and `Save` wrote it unconditionally, which would
wipe the backfilled rank. It now keeps the stored value, matching
`Question.Ordr`. Emberfall pins this.

**Read paths.**

- `FindQuestionsByFismaSystem` selects, sorts by and scans
`functions.ordr`, so `function.order` reaches the payload.
- `FindAnswers` (xlsx export) sorts by `functions.ordr` ahead of
`functionid`, matching the questionnaire.
- `FindFunctions` gains a `functionid` tiebreak, since editions now
share an `ordr`.
- `/scores/aggregate` sorted pillars by `pillarid` (insertion order:
Devices first) while the questionnaire used `pillars.ordr` (Identity
first). It now sorts by `pillars.ordr` with `pillarid` as tiebreak. The
Pillar Scores cards, radar axes and System Detail snapshot render this
array as-is once #741 lands.

The new sort keys move 0 rows on existing data: the backfill sets
`functions.ordr = questions.ordr`, so the key can only break ties a
forked question creates.

## The seed

`_test_data_empire.sql` had every `ordr` at 0, and the migrations match
none of its fictional names. It now carries ranks mirroring 0056:
pillars in CISA order (**Identity, Devices, Networks, Applications,
Data, CrossCutting**), questions banded as `pillar_rank * 100 + index`.
Its pillarids are deliberately not in that order (Identity is 6), as in
the real catalog.

**Five Emberfall arrays move**: three `/questions` pillar arrays and two
`include_pillars=true` aggregate arrays. They previously read
Devices-first only because every `ordr` was 0 and the query fell back to
`questionid`; the frontend re-sorted that payload, so no user saw it.
Everything else is unmodified.

## Verification

- `make test-integration` green.
`TestFunctionOrderingMigrationIntegration` runs 0056 and 0062 on
canonically-named fixtures: copied rank across two editions, the
unrankable case, a pre-set rank left alone, idempotency, the NULL row,
and a down that reverts only what up set.
- `make test-e2e` green, 264 cases, 0 failures.
- Tested locally together with ztmf-ui#741 against production-like data
migrated through 0062: the questionnaire rail, Pillar Scores cards and
radar, System Detail snapshot and score diff all render in CISA pillar
order and questionnaire question order.

## Deploy

**Merge and deploy this before ztmf-ui#741.** #741 deletes the
client-side sorts on the Pillar Scores page and System Detail snapshot
and relies on this PR's aggregate ordering; without it those pages fall
back to `pillarid` order.

Smoke after deploy: pillars return Identity → … → Cross Cutting with
non-zero `order`, and a `PUT /functions/{id}` omitting `"order"` leaves
the stored rank alone.

ztmf-insights needs nothing: no columns are added or changed, and the
nightly merge picks up the new values.

## Out of scope

- No `NOT NULL` on `functions.ordr`; that is a schema change with its
own ztmf-insights reconciliation.
- The duplicate-function probe from the issue feeds #394's constraint
design, not this code.

commits.message:
feat(misc#345): PR checks no longer deploy; DEV deploys from merge, ahead of PROD (#604)

Part of
[ztmf-misc#345](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/345)
· Part of
[ztmf-misc#321](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/321)

### Summary

Cuts over to per-PR environments. A PR to main no longer deploys to DEV;
it runs the same analysis, migration guards, integration tests, image
build, Snyk image scan, and Emberfall smoke as before, and its preview
runs in its own PR environment. DEV now deploys only from a merge to
main, and PROD deploys only after DEV succeeds. Companion PR in ztmf-ui:
[ui!755](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui/pull/755).

### Changes

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `backend.yml` | New `deploy` input (default `true`). With `false`, the
build job runs without a GitHub environment and tags the image locally,
and the ECR push, Lambda build and update, and SSM tag write are
skipped. Tests and scans run either way. |
| `orchestration-dev.yml` | Now "PR checks": calls `backend.yml` with
`deploy: false`, drops the `infrastructure` job, and adds a `PR checks
passed` job that fails if any check failed. |
| `orchestration-prod.yml` | On merge: analysis, then Backend DEV and
Infrastructure DEV, then Backend PROD and Infrastructure PROD. Each PROD
job waits on DEV. |
| `manual-deploy-dev.yml`, `README.md` | Describe the new flow. |

### Decisions

- **DEV before PROD in one workflow,** not a separate push-to-main DEV
deploy. Infrastructure changes no longer reach DEV before merge, so this
ordering is what stops a bad apply before PROD. It adds the DEV deploy
time to every merge, and a failed DEV deploy holds PROD until it is
fixed or re-run.
- **One required check.** A skipped reusable-workflow job reports under
the caller's name (`Backend`), and a run one under nested names
(`Backend / Integration Tests`), so neither can be required without
leaving PRs pending. `PR checks passed` always reports and is the check
the ruleset requires.
- **No environment on PR builds,** so PR checks record no DEV
deployments and the DEV deployment history is merges only.
- **Migration guards kept.** The misc#303 currency check stays as the
merge-ordering guard. The misc#298 missing-migrations check is now
mostly redundant, since PR environments build from the PR merged with
main; it stays for now and can go in a follow-up.

### Ruleset

The `main` ruleset's "require deployment to DEV" rule goes, since
nothing deploys DEV from a PR anymore. It is replaced with required
checks `PR checks passed`, `Build PR API image`, and `Deploy PR
environment`. The ruleset change is made right before this merges.

### Verified

- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration`, and `make test-e2e` pass.
- actionlint is clean apart from the existing `queue: max` keys it does
not know yet.
- This PR's own run is the test of the PR-checks path: no DEV deployment
recorded, deploy steps skipped, `PR checks passed` green.

### Not verified

- The merge path (DEV then PROD) runs for the first time on this PR's
merge.

### Bake

Both flows ran side by side from 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-05 with no
PR-environment failures and a clean nightly reaper.

that groups by pillar in first-appearance order, which is the server's

useQuestionBreakdown carries pillars.ordr and functions.ordr through its

built by walking /scores, not the ordered /questions - but the keys are now
the API's. Its secondary key had been functionName.localeCompare, so within

fix(ui#750): state the email length rule and stop claiming sends that did not happen (#752)

* fix(EmailModal): enforce minimum character length for email subject and body fields

* fix(EmailModal): address review feedback on validation and copy

* **Validation messaging:** Both validation helpers now explicitly state minimum length requirements up front. Previously, length constraints were displayed only after a validation error occurred, failing to meet acceptance criteria.
* **Duplicate submission prevention:** `canSend` functioned as the sole guard for the submission handler, allowing double-clicks to dispatch duplicate POST requests. The button `disabled` property now evaluates `isPending`, and `submitEmail` short-circuits via a ref guard. The ref guard is necessary because `isPending` state updates lag by one render frame, allowing rapid secondary clicks to execute before the button disables.
* **Accessibility improvements and copy formatting:** Input elements now include `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` attributes referencing existing `Field` component IDs. Error state evaluation is deferred until input blur to prevent `role="alert"` regions from announcing incomplete values during typing. Display labels resolve user-facing copy to human-readable text (e.g., "System Delegate" instead of `SYSTEM_DELEGATE`), ensuring raw backend enum keys are restricted to network payloads.

commits.message:
refactor(misc#358): move the three light writes onto useMutation (#751)

* refactor(mutations): move the three light writes onto useMutation

The mass-email send, the data-call create and the target-maturity save each
called axios from their component. They now go through a fetcher and a hook
in the domain module, matching the shape the utils migration established.

Each hook owns invalidation and nothing else. The data-call create
invalidates the data-call prefix and the target-maturity save invalidates
that one system's detail key. The mass-email send invalidates nothing,
because it changes no server state this app reads, and its doc comment says
so rather than leaving the omission to be guessed at.

Two of those invalidations reach nothing today. The layout still holds the
data-call list in component state and the detail page still resolves its
system out of Outlet context, so the existing onCreated and onSaved
callbacks are what actually refresh the screen. Both are kept, with a
comment at each end, so this change alters no behavior. They come out
together when those reads become queries.

The hand-rolled submitting and isSaving flags are gone in favor of
isPending. Leaving a second source of in-flight truth beside a mutation is
the thing the grid migration would have copied three more times.

The target-maturity fetcher returns undefined rather than throwing when a
200 carries no record, so the card keeps showing its own message for that
case instead of the generic network one.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#358

* fix(datacalls): reset the create mutation when the modal closes

Swapping the hand-rolled submitting flag for isPending lost a reset. The
modal stays mounted across opens and takes `open` as a prop, so the old
close-reset effect cleared the flag while the mutation's pending state now
survives. Closing during a create and reopening showed a disabled
"Creating..." button over an empty form until the first request settled.

Calling reset on the same open->false edge restores it. Adds the first test
suite this component has had: the create round trip, a 400 field map landing
on the Name field, and the close-and-reopen case above.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#358

* test(datacalls): model the duplicate-name error the backend actually sends

The duplicate-name case was written against a 400 carrying a
{ data: { field: reason } } map. This endpoint never sends that. A duplicate
maps to model.ErrNotUnique, which the controller returns as a 400 with the
text in `error` and no map, so parseApiError yields a message and the modal
toasts it. The old test passed while proving nothing about the real path.

Splits it in two: the real shape, asserting the toast and that nothing lands
under the Name field, and the field-map shape, which pins the inline branch
rather than the endpoint. No datacall error returns a map today, so that
branch is unreachable from here; the test says so instead of implying
otherwise.

Adds the case behind a question this raised: a create started before the
modal closes still completes and still reports. Closing is not a cancel.
The write is already on its way and aborting would not un-commit it, so it
runs to completion and the caller still learns the outcome.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#358
